newsitem.title: USA: Avis faces charges of bias against Jews - report.
newsitem.headline: Avis faces charges of bias against Jews - report.

text.p: HFS Inc Avis Rent-A-Car, under fire for charges of racial bias at a franchise, now faces allegations from former employees who say they were told to discriminate against Jews, USA Today reported Wednesday.

Ex-workers at Avis' customer service center in Tulsa, Okla., alleged that as recently as last month, supervisors told them to avoid giving corporate accounts or discounts to certain Jewish-owned businesses, the newspaper said.
Six former Avis workers from the corporate accounts department known as Telesales alleged they were told to "watch out for yeshivas," a Hebrew word meaning school, it added.
Workers said it became the code word for businesses owned by ultra-orthodox Jews.
"Telesales agents used the word 'yeshiva' to refer to Hasidic Jews," former employee Elaine Rodgers said in a sworn declaration filed Monday in Raleigh, N.C., USA Today reported.
Agents who worked in the 15-employee department allege they were told to listen for accents and be suspicious of callers from heavily Jewish areas, such as New York, it said.

Rodgers worked for Avis in Tulsa from January 1991 until last summer, when she left voluntarily. Her statement about "yeshivas" was part of her testimony for a racial-bias suit filed in North Carolina, the paper said.
USA Today quoted John Carley, chief counsel for Avis, as saying the rental car company has never had a policy to discriminate against Jews.

Carley said that around 1990 there was a concern that callers to the Tulsa center, claiming to be affiliated with yeshivas, were setting up corporate accounts, allowing persons under 25 to drive the cars and bringing the cars back damaged.
Tulsa agents were alerted to the problem, USA Today said.
Late last year, three black women filed a class action suit against Avis and a longtime franchisee, charging racial bias. The case is pending.
Avis was acquired by HFS Inc in October. An HFS spokeswoman said the Parsippany, N.J.-based company was preparing a response to the newspaper report.
HFS's stock was off 1-3/8 to 66 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
